messages:
alex_j: Heads-up — I'm seeing a reproducible packaging edge-case with the Python SDK. When trying to do a local editable install (Poetry 1.4 + pip 23.x) in a fresh venv, pip/poetry sometimes pulls a cached wheel and the installed package is missing py.typed and some async typing stubs. Breaks mypy + runtime typing checks. Anyone seen this?

mira_k: What exact steps + pyproject.toml? can you paste a minimal repro?

alex_j: Minimal repro:
```bash
# workspace A: build and wheel to simulate cached wheel
git clone git@github.com:redwood/inference-python-sdk tmp/sdk
cd tmp/sdk
# bump version to 0.1.2 locally, build a wheel and populate pip cache
python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install build
.venv/bin/python -m build -w
# move wheel into pip cache dir (or just leave it built so subsequent pip finds it)

# workspace B: fresh venv and try to install editable from path
python -m venv /tmp/testenv && /tmp/testenv/bin/pip install -e /path/to/tmp/sdk
# result: pip reports installing from wheel cache (name-0.1.2-py3-none-any.whl) and installed package has no py.typed file
```

pip debug shows: picks wheel from cache when same name+version exists rather than performing PEP 660 editable build.

samuel: I ran into similar with PEP 660 and pip cache before. If you pre-built a wheel that lacks package data (py.typed), pip will happily reuse it. The resolver will treat the path package as satisfied by that wheel if versions match.

priya: Workarounds we've used: `pip install --no-binary=:all: -e .` or clear the cache (`pip cache purge`) before testing local edits. With Poetry, `poetry add ../path --editable` can behave differently and sometimes creates a lock entry pointing to a tarball or pypi if versions align.

alex_j: Full pip install log snippet: 
```
Defaulting to user installation because normal site-packages is not writeable
Processing /path/to/tmp/sdk
Requirement already satisfied: attrs>=19.2.0 in /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages (from some-dep)
Using cached /home/runner/.cache/pip/wheels/redwood_sdk-0.1.2-py3-none-any.whl
Installing collected packages: redwood-sdk
  Attempting uninstall: redwood-sdk
    Found existing installation: redwood-sdk 0.1.2
    Uninstalling redwood-sdk-0.1.2:
      Successfully uninstalled redwood-sdk-0.1.2
Successfully installed redwood-sdk-0.1.2
# Inspecting package: missing redwood_sdk/py.typed file
```

mira_k: If the cached wheel truly lacks py.typed, that's a packaging problem. We should ensure py.typed is included in the wheel (PEP 561) and that package data is declared. Check pyproject's include config or MANIFEST.in depending on build-backend.

samuel: Agreed. Two-pronged fix: 1) ensure packaging always ships py.typed (and any typing stubs) in built artifacts, 2) add CI test that verifies wheel contents before publishing. Also document clearing cache when doing local editable dev workflows.

priya: I opened a quick ticket and started a tiny PR draft to add py.typed marker file into package and update pyproject include. Also added a GH Action to `python -m zipfile -l dist/*.whl` and assert py.typed present. PR in devex/packaging-fixes.

ci-bot: CI note: tests failing on nightly run (typing/ mypy): `tests/type_checks.py::test_mypy` — error is "Missing py.typed marker". Will re-run after PR lands.

alex_j: For completeness: we should also mention platform-specific wheel tags — if a cached wheel is platform-specific and local editable is pure-Python, pip might still pick cache. For matrix devs (mac arm / linux), recommend building manylinux wheels in CI and not relying on local cached wheels for editable dev.

mira_k: I'll open the PR to add packaging fixes + small CONTRIBUTING note: "when testing editable installs, run `pip cache purge` or use `pip install --no-binary=:all:` to force source-editable build". Also add a small tox/env matrix entry to run an editable install smoke test.

samuel: one more thought — we may want to add a tiny `dev` script in the repo: `scripts/dev_install.sh` which runs `pip cache dir && pip cache purge && python -m pip install -e .` so contributors don't accidentally pick up stale wheels.

priya: Thanks all — I pushed the packaging change and CI check to the branch. folks: if you can run `pip cache dir` + `pip debug --verbose` and paste if you still hit the issue.

alex_j: Great, thanks. I'll test the branch on macOS ARM tonight and report back.
